precepts.text: Abedmelech's deliverance is tied back to the moment the king commanded him to lift Jeremiah out of the miry dungeon before he perished.
precepts.point: But in that day He will deliver Abedmelech, who shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, and shall not fall by the sword, because he has put his trust in the Most High; the Most High deals with the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah, sent to take the prophet up out of the dungeon before he died.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
The Lord deals with Abedmelech the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah. In the chapter before: “Then the king commanded Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.”

Abedmelech was sent to take the prophet up out of the miry dungeon before he perished. So while Jeremiah is still shut up in the court of the prison, the word comes for the Ethiopian: the Lord will bring his words upon the city for evil, but in that day he will deliver Abedmelech; he shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, nor fall by the sword, because he put his trust in the Lord. His deliverance is tied back to the moment the king commanded him to lift Jeremiah out.

points: One of our forefathers was thrown in a pit: they cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah and let him down with cords, and in the dungeon there was no water, but mire; that is dung. Jeremiah sunk in the mire. And Ebedmelech the Ethiopian went to the king: these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, and he is like to die for hunger. The Lord made a way for him, because Jeremiah was set: I am not holding back my tongue anymore, the fire is shut up in my bones; I have to bring the correction and warn the king despite my life. When you step before a king with unpleasant words, as a messenger you might forfeit your life on the spot.

Captain: people might think the Bobby Seale video was just the sixties; we are reading that Jeremiah was in a dungeon, a hole, where the dung came up and he could not avoid it. The same thing, scripturally; it is not far fetched. The Lord constantly reminds us of the mission: do not get comfortable here; you are set on a task. Just as the nations chose their champion, we must constantly declare our champion, Christ the King, the black Messiah. Stay on the mission.

As we go through this class, men and women in this truth: you are going to have to make a choice, and the hardest thing you will have to fight is you. You will tell yourself it is not worth going ten times more for God, that you do not have to get your wife and your kids in order. The hardest person to fight is you, fighting your sins and the things that will keep you from the kingdom. We all need to get ourselves together before that sky cracks.

points: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur hear Jeremiah telling the people that whoever remains in the city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes forth to the Chaldeans shall live and have his life for a prey.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: The princes tell the king that Jeremiah must be put to death because he weakens the hands of the men of war and seeks not the welfare of the people but their hurt; the king answers that he is in their hand and the king can do nothing against them.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: The king swears secretly that as the Most High liveth he will not put him to death nor give him into the hand of those who seek his life.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: If the king refuses to go forth, Jeremiah shows him that all the women left in the king's house shall be brought out to the king of Babylon's princes, saying his friends have prevailed against him and his feet are sunk in the mire and turned away back.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: All his wives and children shall be brought to the Chaldeans, and he shall not escape but be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon and cause the city to be burned with fire.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: We are now getting close to 587 BC, when the Babylonians completely destroyed the temple. Jeremiah was one of the Levites, and Levi was scattered throughout the different areas; look at how Israel treats him in his own land. “Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city”, “for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt.”

It came off as if Jeremiah was not about his race, but in fact he really was; he was just telling them the truth. That is how it is today. It comes off that these Israelites don’t really care about black brothers, about black women. But we do. We are telling you what the Most High says, whether it hurts your feelings or not. ‘Have I become your enemy because I tell you the truth?’ That is how Israel took Jeremiah’s message: he does not seek the welfare of his people, but their hurt.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Ebed-melech “took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.” By this time they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon and barely fed him. He is malnourished, he is not being fed, so Ebed-melech the Ethiopian tells him, “Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords”: put the rags under your armpits and hold on so you can come up. “So they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon”, malnourished, climbing up out of the dungeon.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “Then Zedekiah the king sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet unto him”, “I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.” When you read the chapters earlier, Zedekiah put Jeremiah in prison, and he put him there because he knew the people who did not like Jeremiah wanted to kill him. Now Zedekiah is coming to Jeremiah privately and speaking to him.
“If I declare it unto thee, wilt thou not surely put me to death?” Aren’t you still going to kill me? And Zedekiah “sware secretly unto Jeremiah” that he would not put him to death.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon’s princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house”. Humble yourself, Zedekiah, to the king of Babylon. That is all Zedekiah had to do: listen, and the city would not be burned with fire. But he did not obey Jeremiah’s words. “But if thou wilt not go forth”, the city shall be given to the Chaldeans, “and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand.”

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews”. What did he say? I am afraid of the Jews. Zedekiah was afraid of the people, of what they were going to think of him. It goes to show you what kind of king he was. At the end of the day David stood by the Most High’s word; even in his mistakes he still stayed faithful. Zedekiah’s decisions were based on appeasing the people.

That is not the type of leaders we have to be. We have to always remain faithful to the Most High. That is why we are in the street even though Israel is coming against it. ‘Why do you teach so rough? Why do you scream so loud?’ Because that is what the Most High says; we follow whatever the Most High tells us.
Jeremiah answers, “They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the Lord”: obey the voice of the Most High, “so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.”

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “But if thou refuse to go forth”: if you refuse, Zedekiah, to humble yourself to the king of Babylon, all the women left in the king’s house shall be brought out, and “they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.”
This is talking about 587, 586 BC, when they completely annihilated the city and the temple that Solomon built, took all the Jews out, and only left the poor of the land.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.” If the princes come and ask, Jeremiah is to say, “I presented my supplication before the king”. The princes came and asked him, and he told them as the king commanded, “So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not perceived.” The Jews never perceived what the conversation was between Zedekiah and Jeremiah. “So Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken”.
